records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How slowly the mean wind speed follows the weather target (a front arrives over this time).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How slowly the wind direction swings to a new direction.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Time constant for the wave height to GROW towards a rougher target (about 3x this to reach 95 percent).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Time constant for the waves to SUBSIDE; larger than the build time because a sea dies away slowly.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How slowly the wave direction turns after the wind has turned (the old sea lingers).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Time constant for rain to set in.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Time constant for rain to ease off.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Time constant for storminess and fog.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Extra wind speed at the peak of a gust, as a fraction of the mean wind, at full gustiness.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How far the wind direction veers during a gust (also tilts the rain).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How long a gust fired by hand (key G) takes to die away.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Extra boat speed at the peak of a gust (sails drawing harder). 0 turns the effect off.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Presentation gain on the wave height so storms read clearly at the camera distance.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Crest sharpness in a calm sea (1 = plain sine).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Crest sharpness in a gale: peaked crests, flat troughs.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Weight of the wave height in the sea-state index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Weight of the mean wind speed in the sea-state index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Weight of storminess in the sea-state index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Wave height that counts as a full sea in the index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Wind speed that counts as a full gale in the index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Sea-state index below which the sea is Calm.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Below this the sea is Breezy.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Below this the sea is Rough; above it Gale.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: At or above this the Gale is called a Storm.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Master strength of the ship's roll, pitch and heave on screen (key M cycles off / half / full).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Roll limit (waves plus wind heel).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Pitch limit.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Heave limit.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Natural roll period of the hull: how fast it answers a wave.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Natural pitch period.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Natural heave period.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Damping ratio of all three motions (0.6 = a couple of visible overshoots).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How closely the hull follows the wave slope under it (1 = like a cork).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Wind heel on a beam reach: degrees per squared wind speed in m/s.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Vertical speed of the water meeting the bow above which it throws spray.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Same for the rails (sides of the hull).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Shortest time between spray bursts from one point of the hull in a moderate sea.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Same in a gale.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: No spray bursts below this sea-state index.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How slowly the sail answers a change of wind or sailing angle (period of the damped spring that fills it). Larger = slower, heavier cloth.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Damping of the sail filling: lower = a gust makes it overshoot and settle, higher = it just eases in.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How far a full sail bellies to leeward, in art pixels (the pixel-art silhouette is kept; keep this small).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Below this wind the sail hangs slack.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: From this wind the sail is fully filled (if it is not luffing).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How much a gust fills the sail beyond its steady shape.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How much a gale pulls the sail flat and taut (less belly, not more).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Largest flutter of a luffing sail, in art pixels.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How fast flutter builds up.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How slowly flutter dies away.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Flutter rate in very light wind.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Flutter gets faster with the wind by this much per knot.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How much the ARRIVAL of a gust (wind rising fast) makes the sail shiver once.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Slow breathing of the sail in light air (sub-pixel, so it moves only now and then).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Main period of that breathing (a second, unrelated period is mixed in so it never repeats).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Fall speed of a raindrop in scene metres per second (light rain 15 percent slower, heavy rain 15 percent faster).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Length of a streak in heavy rain (light rain is about half of it).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: How much of the wind speed the falling drops pick up sideways.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Extra sideways drift inside a gust patch (the rain bends where the gust is).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Scale on how many of the simulated drops are visible. 1 = the default look; lower for a cleaner sky.

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: In thick fog the fog starts this much closer to the camera (so it reaches the ship).

records.source: H2D-0.2 weather, sea state and ship response; first values tuned by simulation, confirm by eye in Godot
records.note: Densest the fog may get. H2D-0.2 allowed 0.09, which erased the ship. At 0.02 thick fog hides about 60 percent of the ship's colour and nearly all of the far sea.
